paragraphs: Children in care across Falkirk are looked after by Falkirk Council's own fostering service, part of its Fostering, Adoption and Kinship Care service, alongside the agencies shown above. The council's fostering pages also cover kinship care and short breaks.

Falkirk Council says it would love to hear from anyone thinking about fostering who believes they could make a difference, and it describes children in Falkirk and nearby areas who need a caring home. Its invitation extends to people who simply have questions, so you do not need every answer before getting in touch.

On money, the Scottish Government sets a Scottish Recommended Allowance for foster and kinship carers, intended to make payments more consistent and transparent across the country. For 2026 to 2027 it is £177.68 a week for children aged 0 to 4, £206.71 for ages 5 to 15, and £283.35 for young people aged 16 and over. For foster carers, a fee set by the fostering service is paid on top of the allowance, so it is worth asking each service what it offers.

To start, you can register your interest through Falkirk Council's fostering pages or contact any of the services shown on this page. In Scotland the process usually involves preparation groups, home visits from a social worker and an assessment that can take six to twelve months, before a fostering panel considers your application. You can foster whether you rent or own your home, and you will generally need a spare bedroom.
